'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[Mali War]]
**Five [[Malian Armed Forces|Malian gendarmes]] are killed and four others are wounded in an [[ambush]] on a convoy escorting [[Mining in Mali|mining]] equipment to the [[Australia]]n-owned [[Morila Gold Mine]] in [[Sikasso Region]]. [[Jihadist]] group [[Jama'at Nasr al-Islam wal Muslimin]] claims responsibility for the attack. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/five-gendarmes-killed-attack-mining-convoy-mali-army-2021-09-29/ (Reuters)]
*[[Mohibullah (activist)|Mohibullah]], a prominent [[Rohingya people|Rohingya]] [[Islam|Muslim]] leader and high-profile advocate for the Rohingya, is killed by a gunman in a [[Rohingya refugees in Bangladesh|refugee camp]] in southern [[Bangladesh]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/29/top-rohingya-leader-in-bangladesh-shot-dead (Al Jazeera)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in mainland China]]
****Three [[pet cat]]s who previously tested positive for [[COVID-19]] are [[Animal euthanasia|euthanized]] in the Chinese city of [[Harbin]] amid fears that pets could spread the virus to humans. [https://www.newsweek.com/china-kills-3-pet-cats-which-contracted-covid-amid-fears-they-would-spread-virus-humans-1633899 (Newsweek)]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Singapore]]
****[[Singapore]] reports a record 2,268 new cases of COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide total of confirmed cases to 94,043. [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/singapore/singapore-covid-19-sep-29-8-more-deaths-2268-new-cases-2209956 (CNA)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Europe]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Russia]]
****[[Russia]] reports a record 857 [[COVID-19 pandemic deaths|death]]s from COVID-19 in the past 24 hours, thereby bringing the nationwide death toll to 206,388. [https://www.themoscowtimes.com/2021/09/29/russia-reports-record-virus-deaths-for-second-day-a75166 (''The Moscow Times'')]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in Slovenia]]
****[[Slovenia]] suspends the use of the [[Janssen COVID-19 vaccine]] following the death of a 20-year-old woman who had received the vaccine. [https://www.euronews.com/2021/09/29/slovenia-temporarily-suspends-use-of-johnson-johnson-covid-19-vaccine (Euronews)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Algeria]]
***[[Algeria]] begins producing the [[CoronaVac]] COVID-19 vaccine developed by [[Sinovac]], with expected production of eight million doses per month. [https://www.france24.com/en/live-news/20210929-algeria-begins-sinovac-covid-19-vaccine-production (France 24)]
*[[Holocene extinction]]
**Eleven [[animal species|species]] of [[bird]]s, two [[fish]], one [[bat]], eight [[mussel]]s and one [[plant]] are declared [[extinction|extinct]] by the [[United States Fish and Wildlife Service]]. The [[ivory-billed woodpecker]], the [[Guam flying fox]] and the [[Bachman's warbler]] are among those declared extinct. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-us-canada-58740362 (BBC News)]

'''International relations'''
*[[France–United Kingdom relations]], [[2021 Jersey dispute]]
**[[Jersey]] rejects 75 French fishing applications, once again raising tensions over disputed fishing rights off Jersey. [[France]] condemns the move as French fishermen threaten to impose either a "blockade" of ports, or of lorries travelling to the [[United Kingdom]] via the [[Channel tunnel]], as retaliation. [https://www.dw.com/en/fishing-wars-flare-in-channel-as-jersey-rejects-french-applications/a-59356353 (Deutsche Welle)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Unexplained wealth of the Marcos family]]
**The [[Sandiganbayan]], the [[Philippines]]' anti-graft court, orders Royal Traders Holding Co. Inc., a bank formerly controlled by the late dictator [[Ferdinand Marcos]], to pay the [[Philippine government]] an estimated [[Philippine peso|PHP]]1 billion ([[US dollar|$]]32.446 million) in bank certificates that were confiscated by the [[United States Customs Service]] after Marcos was deposed in 1986. [https://www.rappler.com/nation/sandiganbayan-decision-royal-traders-holding-marcos-ill-gotten-bank-asset (Rappler)]
*[[LGBT rights in Nepal]]
**The [[Central Bureau of Statistics (Nepal)|Central Bureau of Statistics]] adds an option for a [[third gender]] to its census forms for the first time. [https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2021/9/29/nepal-introduces-third-gender-category-in-latest-census (Al Jazeera)]
*[[Britney Spears conservatorship dispute]]
**The [[Los Angeles County Superior Court]] suspends [[James Parnell Spears]] from the [[conservatorship]] of his daughter, American singer [[Britney Spears]], which was implemented in 2008. [https://www.philstar.com/entertainment/2021/09/30/2130788/britney-spears-father-removed-her-guardian (AFP via ''The Philippine Star'')]
*[[September 2021 Guayaquil prison riot]]
**The death toll from yesterday's [[prison riot|riot]] between rival [[prison gang|gangs]] at a [[prison]] in [[Guayaquil]], [[Ecuador]], increases to 116, making the incident the deadliest prison riot in the [[history of Ecuador|country's history]]. [https://www.bbc.com/news/world-latin-america-58733202 (BBC News)]
*The [[United States Department of the Treasury|U.S. Treasury Department]], in coordination with [[Qatar]], imposes sanctions on [[United Arab Emirates]] [[real estate]] company [[Aldar Properties]] and seven residents of [[Bahrain]], Qatar and [[Saudi Arabia]] for allegedly financing [[Hezbollah]]. [https://www.aljazeera.com/economy/2021/9/29/us-issues-hezbollah-related-sanctions-in-coordination-with-qatar (Al Jazeera)]

'''Politics and elections'''
*[[Politics of Japan]]
**[[2021 Liberal Democratic Party (Japan) leadership election|2021 Liberal Democratic Party leadership election]]
***The [[Liberal Democratic Party (Japan)|Liberal Democratic Party]] elects former foreign minister [[Fumio Kishida]] as its new leader. Kishida is expected to become prime minister within days, succeeding [[Yoshihide Suga]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/japans-ruling-party-votes-new-leader-who-will-almost-certainly-be-next-pm-2021-09-28/ (Reuters)]
*[[Indigenous land rights in Australia]]
**The [[Queensland]] [[Queensland Government|state government]] grants [[Indigenous land rights|land rights]] over parts of the [[UNESCO]]-listed [[Wet Tropics of Queensland|Wet Tropics]], including the [[Daintree National Park]], to the [[Kuku Yalanji]] people. The Kuku Yalanji will initially co-administer the land with the Queensland government. [https://www.theguardian.com/australia-news/2021/sep/29/indigenous-traditional-owners-win-back-daintree-rainforest-in-historic-deal (''The Guardian'')]
*[[Politics of Tunisia]]
**[[Tunisian President]] [[Kais Saied]] appoints [[Najla Bouden Romdhane]] as the first female prime minister in [[Tunisia]] and the Arab world. [https://www.cnn.com/2021/09/29/africa/tunisia-prime-minister-najla-bouden-romdhane-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Science and technology'''
*[[COVID-19 misinformation]]
**[[YouTube]] says that it will ban misinformation related to all [[Vaccine|vaccines]]. [https://techcrunch.com/2021/09/29/youtube-will-now-ban-content-with-vaccine-misinformation/ (TechCrunch)]
**[[Russia]] threatens to ban [[YouTube]] if it does not reinstate two German-language channels backed by the Russian state that were deleted for violating COVID-19 misinformation guidelines. [https://www.bbc.com/news/technology-58737433 (BBC News)]
